To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the minimal single-fermionic extension of Lorentz and $CPT$ violating QED is renormalizable, and that the anomaly coefficients vanish provided invariance under $C$ (or $PT$) transformations is imposed.

(i) the single-fermionic extension of the standard QED is renormalizable at all orders of the perturbative expansion; (ii) the gauge anomaly coefficients do not vanish, in general, but they do vanish provided the theory is invariant under the discrete symmetries $C$, $P$ and $T$ (i.e. the $CPT$-symmetry).

(1) the minimal single-fermionic QED extension is renormalizable; (2) it is stable; (3) the gauge anomaly is absent if invariance under C and/or PT transformations is imposed; (4) invariance under $CPT$ transformations is a necessary but not sufficient condition for renormalizability; (5) invariance is not a sufficient condition for stability.
